title: The Evening Brief: City guilty, Powers leaves, Beckham out, Reed sidelined
dek: Thursday brought four significant personnel and legal developments across sports: Manchester City found guilty of 114 financial charges, Arizona State's hockey coach placed on leave, the Giants released Odell Beckham Jr., and the Packers lost their leading receiver for the season.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Multiple programs face accountability crises, some legal, some institutional, some roster-related, that will test leadership decisions in the coming weeks and months.
bottom_line: Thursday brought accountability moments across four institutions: Manchester City's guilty verdict stands pending appeal by Friday, with sanctions undetermined and due by end of January; Arizona State's independent-investigation deadline arrives October 9; the Packers lost their leading receiver for the season; and Dillon Brooks faces arraignment October 28 during the Suns' opening month. Each case enters a procedural next stage where evidence and institutional response will determine consequences.
body: Manchester City's independent commission verdict stands as the most consequential administrative ruling in Premier League history, though the sanctions remain undetermined. The panel found the club guilty of 114 of 115 financial charges spanning 2009-2018, concluding that sham sponsorship deals and disguised owner funding artificially increased revenues and reduced costs by more than 900 million pounds over the nine-year period. The commission detailed specific schemes: one involving a modified sponsorship agreement in May 2013 that plugged a 9.9 million pound gap to comply with UEFA rules within days of the financial year-end, and the Fordham Arrangement, which recorded artificially inflated image-rights payments. Manchester City denies the findings and has until Friday, October 4, to file its appeal. The Premier League's new rules require an appeal hearing within 12 weeks of the deadline, with judgment due by the end of January 2027. The commission has authority to impose points deductions, transfer embargoes, or expulsion. The honest read on the evidence is stark: the reporting shows the panel found the club made concerted efforts to frustrate the investigation and that factual witnesses provided false testimony. What remains open is what penalties follow, and whether the verdict reshapes English football competition or becomes precedent without systemic teeth.

At Arizona State, the collapse of sophomore Matthew Mayich on August 20 during an outdoor workout in 89-degree heat without cold water available continues to trigger institutional pressure. Coach Greg Powers was placed on paid administrative leave on September 30, three days before the season opener, after seven anonymous rostered players sent a 26-page letter to university president Michael Crow disputing the school's preliminary account and calling for an independent investigation. The players cited fear of retaliation for speaking out. Mayich's family attorney separately asserted that placing Powers on leave while his "best friend of the last decade stays in charge of the locker room doesn't solve the problem." Assistant coach Mike Corbett will lead the Sun Devils in their Friday opener against Lindenwood. Despite the leave, no independent investigation has been launched. The Arizona State Police Department is conducting an internal review, and the Maricopa County Attorney declined to take over. Two Arizona Republican state lawmakers requested the Board of Regents retain an independent investigator, with an October 9 deadline for response. U.S. Senators Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego called for a full outside investigation. The case mirrors 2024's Tufts men's lacrosse "Navy SEAL Workout" that caused exertional rhabdomyolysis in 24 players. Whether the Board of Regents' October 9 response commits to external accountability will clarify whether ASU's internal process satisfies the pressure from players, family, and elected officials.

In the NFL, the Packers lost their leading receiver for the entire 2026 season. Jayden Reed, who signed a 50.25 million dollar contract extension in April, suffered a neck injury on the second play of Green Bay's Week 2 game against the New York Jets on September 20 and will undergo surgery. Reed was placed on injured reserve on September 30. Coach Matt LaFleur confirmed the move on Wednesday. The team addressed the loss by signing 15-year veteran guard Kevin Zeitler, a Wisconsin native and 2023 Pro Bowl selection who has played 214 regular-season games with 213 starts since 2012, more than any other offensive lineman during that span. The Packers also signed defensive tackle David Blay Jr. and wide receiver Coleman Owen to the practice squad.

The New York Giants released wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. after three games and zero catches on 20 offensive snaps. Beckham, who ranks second in Giants franchise history in receiving yards with 5,476 and fourth in touchdowns with 44, returned to the team that drafted him in 2014 with hopes to "rewrite the last bit of the chapter," but head coach John Harbaugh said the team could not generate production from the spot. "Roster-wise, we need more out of that spot," Harbaugh stated. The Giants signed wide receiver and punt returner Braxton Berrios to the active roster and added Charlie Jones, addressing the team's need to place Berrios on the active roster after he exhausted his practice-squad elevations. Beckham, who turns 34 in November, will seek employment elsewhere as a free agent.

Phoenix's Dillon Brooks was formally charged on September 30 with a Class 1 misdemeanor DUI liquor/drugs/vapors/combo stemming from a March 6 traffic stop in Scottsdale. Brooks is scheduled for arraignment on October 28, approximately one week after the Suns open their regular season. Bodycam footage from the stop shows Brooks blew a 0.0 on a breathalyzer, creating a factual tension: the charge cites impairment, but the equipment reading contradicts that. An officer noted Brooks's vehicle smelled "like a dispensary." Brooks told the officer he had not smoked in six months. Brooks joined the Suns in 2025, averaged 20.2 points per game in his first season, and signed a three-year, 73 million dollar extension over the summer. The tension between the breathalyzer result and the DUI charge will likely become central to the case; prosecutors must justify their decision based on evidence beyond alcohol or explain what other testing supported the claim.
